summary: 1933 Civilian Conservation Corps tower and lookout house near Montgomery Creek; a later site note says it was destroyed before 1972.

facts.design: timber tower with a lookout house
facts.status_note: Destroyed sometime before 1972, according to a site note.

events.note: Civilian Conservation Corps crew from the Squaw Creek camp was building the tower and lookout house in August 1933; a site note gives a 24-foot timber tower
Lookout in the charge of E. Sims, as reported in October 1933

evidence.quote: Little Round Mountain (LO site), Shasta County, California

evidence.supports: in Shasta-Trinity National Forest, elevation 3,020 ft
evidence.quote: In Shasta-Trinity National Forest, Elevation = 3020 ft.
The lookout here was on a 24 foot high timber tower built in 1933

evidence.supports: August 1933 report: CCC crew building 26-foot tower and lookout house near Montgomery Creek
evidence.quote: a crew of ten men from the Squaw Creek C. C. C. camp are constructing a twenty-six foot tower and lookout house on Little Round Mountain near Montgomery creek.

evidence.supports: work directed by Melville Still of Mount Shasta
evidence.quote: Under the direction of Melville Still of Mount Shasta

evidence.supports: August 1933 item was from the Dunsmuir News
October 1933 report: 26-foot tower construction under way
evidence.quote: Construction of a lookout house with a 26 foot tower is going ahead on Little Round mountain, near Montgomery Creek.

evidence.supports: October 1933 item was from the Record Searchlight

evidence.quote: Bert Orbell is foreman in charge of the work.

evidence.supports: lookout in charge of E. Sims; to close when rains fall
evidence.quote: The lookout, which is in the charge of E. Sims, will be closed as soon as the rains fall.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Both 1933 reports give a 26-foot tower, which matches the recorded 7.9 m; a later site note gives a 24-foot timber tower. The sources disagree and the height is uncertain.
The site note places the lookout in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest; the record had no agency.

sources.title: Little Round Mountain - Forest Lookouts
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (western US), quoting the Dunsmuir News and Record Searchlight, 1933

notes_for_editor: Height conflict: 1933 press says 26 ft (the record's 7.9 m matches), the site note says 24 ft. Destruction is dated only as before 1972, so no event was written for it. The FFLA list gives this gone site NHLR US 260, but that register page is not in cache. No source describes what remains or whether the site is open.
